markscheme.html:
a.i

Curve within all error bars ✓
Must be one curve. Do not allow multiple lines or straight line dot to dot but be lenient about ‘smoothness’.

a.ii

ALTERNATIVE 1 Curve extrapolated to V-axis and intercept read correctly within half a square ✓
ALTERNATIVE 2 Numerical value calculated 48 cm3 ✓
Unit not required Expect a value of around 48 cm3 but allow ECF from ai) Unit not required Allow range of ±2 cm3

b.i

Proposes workable method used to test suggestion. ✓ e.g. check if the half-life / decay constant is constant OR Constant ratio test for equal time changes using values from graph line OR Value of gradient proportional to V OR fits data from points on curve to ln V = c – kt in some way
Do not allow suggestion of use of plotted points Allow a method which suggest e.g. calculating a half-life and using it to predict another volume

b.ii

Calculations must be from an appropriate method

method correctly uses two data points on graph ✓ method correctly uses three or more data points with suitable correct comment ✓ (leading to statement that foam experiment is a suitable model)
e.g. one half life or decay constant is calculated correctly e.g a second half-life or decay constant is calculated correctly and recognition that they are the same   OR   half-life / decay constant used to predict a volume at another time     Measurements must be checked and within one square vertically / horizontally to the line. Half-life is about 280 s but calculations must be checked

ALTERNATIVE 4 Calculation of final volume of foam  ✓ Attempt to extend graph axis and estimate time Answer in range 780–900 s ✓

question.html:
A foam forms above a liquid when the liquid is stirred or poured.

A student investigates the change in volume of a foam with time.

At time t = 0, the liquid is poured quickly into a measuring cylinder and a foam forms above the liquid. The student waits one minute for the foam to settle and then records the volume V of the foam and the time t.

The student repeats the measurement every minute.

The student plots the data to show how V varies with t. Error bars are given for values of V; errors in t are negligible.

a.i Draw the best-fit line for these data on the graph, extrapolating your line to the V-axis. [1]

a.ii Estimate the initial volume of the foam. [1]

b

The student suggests that the foam experiment can model radioactive decay.

For this to be true, the V–t graph must have similar properties to those of a graph of corrected count rate against time for the decay of a radioactive nuclide.

b.i Explain how data from the V–t graph can be tested to decide whether the foam experiment can model radioactive decay. [1]

b.ii Show, using data from the V–t graph and your test from (b)(i), that the student’s suggestion is correct. [2]

c

The student decides to stop the experiment when the volume of the foam has decreased by th of its original volume.

Predict the time at which the student will stop the experiment.

[2]
